articles.summary: As customers celebrate National Clean Energy Month and prepare for cooler weather, Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) is encouraging customers to take simple steps to reduce energy waste and lower bills. One often-overlooked source of energy comes from "vampire appliances" and electronics that continue drawing power even when turned off, also known as phantom or standby power. Unplugging idle devices and using free tools can help customers identify and reduce this hidden waste. Up to 10% of a home's electricity bill may come from devices that continue drawing power even when turned off, according to Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL). Idle energy loads also account for about 1% of global carbon emissions, according to LBNL. The average U.S. household can spend $100 each year powering electronics that are not being used, according to the Department of Energy (DOE). That number can rise depending on how many always-on devices you have in your home and where you live.
articles.title: Preventing Phantom Power from Taking a Bite out of Your Budget This National Clean Energy Month

The solution also supports confidential computing, helping protect sensitive data during AI processing.
